title: Longevity slopes were uncertain in five bird drought abundance samples from a 2024 release
abstract: We tested whether longer-lived bird species had higher recorded abundance responses to drought after control for body mass. Five samples from a 2024 public release supplied 157 complete records and 129 study-species units in Australia, Hawaii and Spain. Four adjusted slopes were positive and one was negative. All five corrected HC3 working-model intervals included zero. Mass control changed the Spanish slope from -0.422 to +0.293 source effect-size units per tenfold longevity. One-species deletion could change the sign in four samples. The extract did not establish a common longevity advantage. Shared droughts, ancestry, detection, publication bias, missing traits and incomplete annual dates limit inference. Balanced independent-period tests were not supported. No air pollution or causal climate-change effect was tested. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Mass-adjusted longevity slopes in five study samples. Blue lines are five-test corrected HC3 working-model intervals. Orange crosses show unadjusted slopes on the same species. Shared droughts and ancestry can violate the interval assumptions.
